MY Lords, I charge ye in his Highnesse name, To keepe the peace, you, and your followers.
Good M. Sheriffe, look vnto your self. But be briefe, ye were best. Powesse, I thinke thy Welsh and thou do smart. Thy hearts best bloud shall pay the losse of mine. Good M. Maior of Hereford be briefe.
Do so, for we haue other businesse. Hold then, lets heare it. Herbert, I thinke my sword came neere thy heart.
Will ye disturbe the Iudges, and the Assise? Heare the Kings proclamation ye were best. Hold, in the Kings name, hold. Hee's here my Lord. Please it your Lordship, my Lord Powesse is gone, Past all recouery. There are some of them, sirs, lay ho • d on them, Disarme them Bailiffes. And't please your Lordship these are al but one. About religion (as I heard) my Lord. Lord Powesse detracted from the power of Rome, Affirming Wickliffes doctrine to be true, And Romes erroneous: hot reply was made By the lord Herbert, they were traytors all That would maintaine it: Powesse answered, They were as true, as noble, and as wise As he, that would defend it with their liues, He namde for instance sir Iohn Old-castle The Lord Cobham: He • bert replide againe, He, thou, and all are traitors that so hold. The he was giuen, the seuerall factions drawne, And so enragde, that we could not appease it. Sirs, haue ye taken the lord Powesse yet?
